A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SDTrack and have readable, corresponding text, equations, figures and tables. All 11 pages of each were inspected. Neither includes appendices or the Supplementary Materials referenced in the text; the comparison covers the supplied material.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original tracking experiments, event-aggregation comparisons and ablations, including Tables 1–4 and Figures 4–7.

after.justification: The original experimental evaluations remain, and Table 1 adds results for two neuron/timestep variants of SDTrack-Tiny.

M1.justification: V2 extends SDTrack beyond the original I-LIF configuration with LIF and temporally processed I-LIF variants. For multiple iterative timesteps, it divides the event stream into corresponding portions before GTP processing. The principal GTP, IPL, backbone, tracking head and loss designs remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use ImageNet-1K pretraining and evaluate event-based tracking on FE108, FELT and VisEvent. The additional neuron configurations use the existing datasets and task coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator trackers in Table 1, aggregation methods in Figure 4 and candidate backbones in Table 3 are retained. STARK's FELT result changes source, but the comparator itself is unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds LIF 4×1 and I-LIF 2×2 configurations alongside the retained I-LIF configuration now designated 1×4. It replaces STARK's GTP-based FELT comparison with benchmark-sourced results. Section 4.2 also revises the energy-accounting formula to include an explicit self-attention term.

E4.justification: Table 1 adds a comparison of neuron type and iterative versus virtual timestep allocation within SDTrack-Tiny. This tests sensitivity beyond v1's backbone comparisons. Existing GTP sensitivity experiments, IPL/head/pretraining ablations and degraded-condition examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes FELT AUC/PR (%) from 39.6/50.1 to 39.3/51.2 for Tiny and from 39.8/50.7 to 40.0/51.4 for Base. STARK changes from 39.6/51.7 to benchmark-sourced 39.3/50.8, so this is not a same-setting performance decline. Two neuron-variant result rows are added. The retained models' FE108 and VisEvent scores and Tables 2–4 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces the I-LIF firing-rate and binary-spike conversion equations with membrane-update, firing and reset equations intended to encompass IF, LIF and I-LIF neurons. The energy definition also changes. The added IPL block matrix restates the existing diagonal concatenation; no new proof appears in the supplied PDFs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same principal claims: GTP improves event representation, IPL supplies positional information, and SDTrack provides an efficient transformer-based spike-driven tracking baseline with competitive performance.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly asserts independence from specific neuron types. Section 4.3 qualifies the temporal variants' applicability by highlighting weak performance on long-sequence FELT, and removes v1's explanation of STARK's FELT precision advantage through GTP. The mechanisms and limitations discussed in Section 5 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly distinguishes iterative and virtual timesteps, documents event-stream subdivision for multiple iterative steps, and identifies the shared ablation configuration as Tiny with I-LIF 1×4. Hardware, input dimensions, architecture sizes and the future code-release statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The revised neuron background adds Brunel and Van Rossum's integrate-and-fire reference and Maass's spiking-network reference. It removes citations to Spike2former, integer-valued training for object detection, event-driven sparse 3D recognition and SpikeLM. The main tracking-related positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 3.1 is renamed and rewritten, with localized revisions to implementation details, energy accounting and experimental discussion. The overall section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a neuron column, explicit T×D labels and grouped variant rows. Figure 2 corrects its GTP equation references from 2/3 to 4/5. Captions and page placement change locally; all seven figures and four tables are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful neuron/timestep comparisons and clearer implementation information. However, its revised Equation 20 adds self-attention FLOPs directly to energy terms without an energy-per-operation factor, while retaining the original main-model energy values. Its stronger FELT ranking also partly reflects replacing STARK's GTP result with benchmark-sourced evidence, alongside unexplained SDTrack score revisions. These benefits and unresolved reporting issues prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
